summary: Graceful canary swap drops pinned session when client uses chunked/multipart request
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during a scheduled graceful canary swap in us-east-1 their tenant sessions that had explicit model pins are suddenly served by the legacy variant and see degraded outputs. The customer uses a client which uploads prompt payloads using chunked/multipart POSTs (large prompt embedding + attachments).

Impact:
- Several customer requests routed to legacy variant; observed silent fallback (no 5xx) but responses differ (tokenization deltas).
- Streaming sessions for pinned model appear to lose pin mid-stream causing mixed-model outputs for a subset of requests (~0.8% of their traffic) for ~20 minutes during the canary window.

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1; enterprise tenant Acme Health; requests originate from their EU proxy into us-east-1 edge cluster.
- Affected model: gptx-13b-quantized-v2 (pinned at route level).

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Send a multi-part chunked POST containing a large prompt + binary attachment with header X-Tenant-Session and X-Model-Pin set.
2) During a canary weight ramp (10% -> 50%), observe that some requests are routed to legacy variant despite header indicating explicit pin.
3) Replaying with non-chunked single POST preserves pin consistently.

Observed logs / telemetry attached by customer (excerpt):
- edge-proxy: "WARN header_truncated: X-Tenant-Session length 512 > 256 -> dropped-suffix"
- orchestrator: "INFO route_decision: tenant=acme-health session=abc123 fallback=legacy-variant reason=missing_session_affinity"
- serving-runtime: intermittent kv-cache-miss and prewarm handshake failures for sessions that lost pins.

Notes: customer provided request IDs: req-20260310-22A, req-20260310-22B, req-20260310-31C (attached).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:42 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer opened with evidence and request IDs. Reports regressions only during canary windows and only for chunked uploads.
2026-03-10 10:05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Confirmed traces showing header truncation on some chunked requests at ingress-proxy. Marked for deeper ingress review.

2026-03-11 14:17 - Ingrid Park (Edge Eng): Observed X-Tenant-Session sometimes exceeding our internal 256-byte trimming threshold after multipart reassembly. If session token is truncated, orchestrator treats it as new session, dropping pin affinity.

2026-03-12 08:33 - Rahul Desai (Serving Eng): Reproduced locally by sending chunked requests with long session tokens; found that prewarm handshake code path expects session header to be present in initial connect frame — chunked boundary reassembly currently can reorder header delivery during a canary dual-route handshake.

2026-03-13 11:02 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Temporary mitigation deployed in us-east-1 edge pool: increase header buffer limit and treat truncated tokens as 'sticky' if initial fragment included explicit X-Model-Pin. Monitoring for side effects.

2026-03-14 07:55 - Support (Maya): Customer confirmed reduction in incidents after mitigation but still seeing rare (~0.05%) occurrences. Requested ETA for permanent fix and clarification on workaround for their SDK.

2026-03-14 09:10 - Ingrid Park (Edge Eng): Hotfix PR opened to ensure multipart reassembly preserves and reattaches original header values before any routing decision: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingress-proxy/pull/2421. Target canary deploy 2026-03-16.

2026-03-14 12:33 - Rahul Desai (Serving Eng): Noted additional improvement in orchestrator: treat explicit per-request model pin as higher-priority than missing session affinity when weight-slicing during canary rollouts. Will land change behind feature flag to avoid liveness regressions.
investigation_notes: Initial triage showed ingress was trimming long X-Tenant-Session tokens after multipart reassembly. Truncation only surfaced during canary weight shifts because the orchestrator's session affinity check runs early in the routing pipeline and falls back to variant selection when token missing/invalid. Also found a race: prewarm handshake for the new canary variant sometimes completes before the last chunk with headers is processed, which leads to request being accepted and routed without the pin. Reproducible with crafted client sending large session tokens and chunked boundaries that split header-fragment delivery.
workaround: Recommended customer temporary workarounds: 1) Switch to single-part POSTs for pinned-session traffic during canary windows. 2) Shorten session token length (<= 256 bytes) in their SDK. 3) Explicitly pass model parameter in the request body (model: gptx-13b-quantized-v2) until fix is deployed.
next_steps: 1) Merge and canary-deploy ingress-proxy PR to preserve headers across multipart reassembly (PR #2421). 2) Enable orchestrator feature-flag to prefer explicit request model pin over missing session affinity during staged rollouts. 3) Monitor canary (us-east-1) for 72h, compare pin-loss rate against baseline. 4) Postmortem and SDK guidance update if root cause confirmed. Engineering owners: Ingrid Park (Edge), Rahul Desai (Serving).
